author: DTrim99
body:
Confirmed on both counts — PE is over-granting the IT-214 credit, and this household actually fails eligibility twice over. PE misses both gates.

**1. The renter cap ($450/month).** The credit is only for renters whose average monthly rent is $450 or less:

> The average monthly rent you and other members of your household paid was **$450 or less**, not counting charges for heat, gas, electricity, furnishings, or board.

This record's rent is $17,139/year ≈ $1,428/month, well over. PE has the $5,400 annual cap (`max_rent`), but the check compares that cap to **25% of the rent** ($4,285, the line-22 property-tax equivalent) rather than to the rent itself ($17,139) — so it lets annual rent up to $21,600 through. The $450 cap is on the full rent (line 21); the 25% only applies afterward, to size the credit (line 22, "Only 25% of your adjusted rent is considered real property taxes paid"). So the check should test the rent directly.

**2. Household gross income (the $18,000 limit).** The credit is limited to households with gross income of $18,000 or less, and that measure includes **all Social Security**, not just the taxable part:

> The real property tax credit may be available to New York State residents who have **household gross income of $18,000 or less** ...

> [Line 11] Social Security payments not included on line 9, **including all payments received under the Social Security Act** ...

Here that's $6,600 pension + $15,506 Social Security + $4 interest ≈ **$22,110**, over the limit — which is why you couldn't get the $273 even at $5,400 of rent. PE tests **federal AGI** (~$6,600, since the Social Security isn't federally taxable at this income) rather than IT-214 household gross income, so it slips under $18,000.

Either gate alone zeroes the credit for this record; PE misses both. Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9298 — the rent-cap comparison is a one-line fix (`rent` vs the cap, not `25% × rent`); the income gate needs the IT-214 "household gross income" measure (federal AGI plus the nontaxable Social Security / pension add-backs) in place of federal AGI in the credit.

(Source: 2022 Form IT-214 instructions, [it214i_2022.pdf](https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/NY/2022/it214i_2022.pdf).)
